note: Rust mirror of the compensates feature (per-dispatch saga compensation, lib/hecks/bluebook/dsl/process_manager_builder.rb) -- the exact scenario docs/implemented/reference/dispatch.md's own doctest demonstrates: fund a source account, freeze the destination, request a transfer. Account.Debit succeeds and moves the money out; Account.Credit then refuses (the destination is frozen). Settlement's own Account.Debit dispatch declares `compensates Account::Credit`, so the runtime fires that compensation the moment Credit refuses -- the source account's balance ends back at 1000 (not 800), and the saga log names the compensation distinctly (`compensation: true`). This pins that exact instances/events/refusals/reactions/sagas comparison byte-for-byte against Ruby, including the `compensation`/`delivered` tag on the derived Account.Credit compensation entry in `sagas` -- the same log shape spec/rust_conformance_spec.rb's own comparison checks for every other fixture here.
